payload.statement:
# HOL Council — ch22 Reference Sheets

Chapter under review: ch22 (quarto-book/chapters/22-reference-sheets.qmd), "Quick Reference Sheets", 303 lines.

Task: audit the chapter as a publishable unit and produce a disposition plan.
Each member audits through their own lens (see role card) and files a finding:
  stance support = the chapter holds on this lens as written
  stance refute  = the chapter must change; name the fix and its scope
Findings cite [file:line] in the chapter (22-reference-sheets.qmd). Mechanics
findings state the broken value and the expected value. Cross-chapter checks
use the authoritative chapters as the reference, not this chapter (core
rules = ch06: Boon/Bane, success tiers 1-8/9-14/15-18+, Critical/Fumble;
skills = ch07: the 23-skill roster and attribute keys (Athletics Brawn,
Parry Brawn, Acrobatics Agility, Dodge Agility, Endurance Fortitude,
Survival Fortitude, Lore Knowledge, History Knowledge, Arcana Knowledge,
Nature Knowledge, Religion Knowledge, Medicine Reason, Persuasion Guile,
Insight Reason, Deception Guile, Intimidation Brawn, Performance Guile,
Stealth Agility, Sleight of Hand Agility, Thievery Agility, Perception
Reason, Craft Reason, Alchemy Reason); disciplines = ch08: 23 disciplines /
9 categories; combat = ch13: the 21-condition table (incl. Dazzled,
Petrified; Asleep X is "Unaware for X minutes"), Basic Maneuvers (Disengage
5 ft, Aid "+2 on their next roll before your next turn", Shove "Brawn vs
Brawn/Agility", Catch Breath, Command extra move, Stand Up is a MANEUVER),
morale (Strong "Gains +1 on its next attack", auto-triggers: below half HP,
leader defeated, half group fallen, overwhelming force), dying (Critical
wake at half HP, Strong stabilize at 1 HP, Standard stable, Weak still
dying, Fumble death), cover (attacker -1/-3 / full cannot target), action
economy (Action 1 / Movement 1 / Maneuver 1 / Reaction 1 per round / Free
unlimited; trading Action -> Movement or Maneuver, never up); armor/shields
= ch16: DR values + Discipline requirements (Buckler 1 Protection +1 DR,
Shield 1 Protection +2 DR, Tower Shield 2 Protection +3 DR HALF COVER),
Half Plate/Chain Mail/Plate reduce speed 5 ft; advancement = ch18: level
table (L1 4 DP "Class signature, Starting Disciplines", L3 Progression
Discipline + Adept unlock, L5 4 DP "DP windfall" — NO class features exist,
L7 Master unlock, L8 attribute +1, L10 3 DP — no milestone; "Classes do not
have feature upgrades"); GM guidance = ch19: rest rules, encounter
multiplier semantics (a creature's Challenge is its share of the budget —
Easy x1, Standard x2, Hard x3, Deadly x4+ party level, so a level-3 Easy
encounter has budget 3: 6 Wolves C1/2; Standard budget 6: 1 Knight C3 + 6
Guards C1/2; Hard budget 9: 1 Young Dragon C6 + 6 Cultists C1/2; Deadly 12:
1 Ancient Dragon C12); bestiary = ch20: Ancient Dragon (C12) exists,
encounter examples there still need re-totalling to the multiplier budgets;
glossary = ch21: Rest/Recharge/Finesse definitions, PV as defense-roll
bonus, Condition list).

Disposition classes (for the librarian's synthesis):
  mechanical    - safe to implement as a micro-PR (headings, tables, wording,
                  em-dashes, single-cell refs, budget rows, band values,
                  vocabulary swaps, arithmetic)
  substantive   - needs a dispatched implementation pass (multi-file, new
                  content, worked-example rewrite requiring new narrative)
  design-decision - needs Bruce's ruling; implement the recommended default,
                  flagged veto-revertible in decisions-pending.md

Standing book conventions are in force: zero em-dashes in book text; damage
budgets flat 2/4/6 6/9/12 9/15/21 (Novice/Adept/Master, keyed to C1-2/C3-6/
C7+); card costs 2/4/8; Adept prereqs EXACTLY 2, Master EXACTLY 3; L3/L7
gates; no "chain" vocabulary (growing-card model); no "save" vocabulary
(checks); no flat +N damage riders; leveled conditions (Burning X, Slowed X,
Poisoned X, Dazed X, Frozen X, Asleep X); en-dash for prose ranges (50-52 ->
50–52); art-tracker residue ("Placeholder for final art...") is stripped
from captions (ch20 #387 precedent); quick-reference tables abbreviate
legitimately but must never contradict the authoritative chapter or the
sheet's own tables.

payload.argument: Audited the quick-reference chapter cell-by-cell against the authoritative chapters for this round's topics. The chapter largely holds: the 23-skill roster and attribute keys match ch07, the discipline catalog matches ch08's nine categories, and the resolution tiers, difficulty modifiers, action economy, morale, dying, cover, damage budgets, card costs, and armor DR values all agree with ch06/ch13/ch16. Six defects nonetheless block publication, each a quick-reference cell that contradicts its authoritative source: the three encounter examples under-sum their multiplier budgets (they total 2, 4, and 8 where a level-3 party's Easy/Standard/Hard budgets are 3, 6, and 9); the Asleep X row says Unconscious where ch13 says Unaware; the Prone row ends with a move where ch13 and the sheet's own maneuvers list say maneuver; the level table awards class features at 5 and 10 although ch18 has none (level 5 is a DP windfall); the Tower Shield row omits half cover; and the heavy-armor rows omit the 5-ft speed reduction. A hyphenated range on line 228 also breaks the en-dash convention. Because the sheet's stated purpose is to be the numbers used at the table, contradictory cells defeat the chapter's function; all fixes are mechanical row/cell corrections.

evidence.claim: Easy example (22-reference-sheets.qmd:277) lists 4 Wolves at C1/2, totalling budget 2 instead of the x1 party-level budget of 3 for a level-3 party; six wolves are required.
Standard example (22-reference-sheets.qmd:278) lists a Knight plus 2 Guards, totalling 4 against the x2 budget of 6; six guards are required.
Hard example (22-reference-sheets.qmd:279) lists a Young Dragon plus 4 Cultists, totalling 8 against the x3 budget of 9; six cultists are required.
The Asleep X row (22-reference-sheets.qmd:77) labels the sleeper Unconscious, which both contradicts the combat chapter and duplicates the table's own separate Unconscious row at line 97.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asleep X | Unconscious | X minutes or damage

evidence.claim: The combat chapter's condition entry for Asleep X is Unaware, lasting X minutes, waking on damage (13-combat.qmd:169).
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asleep X | Unaware for X minutes | Wakes on damage

evidence.claim: The Prone row (22-reference-sheets.qmd:93) ends via a move, contradicting the combat chapter and the sheet's own maneuvers table at line 70 where standing up is a maneuver.
The combat chapter's Prone row ends via the Stand up maneuver (13-combat.qmd:185).
The level table (22-reference-sheets.qmd:221 and :226) attaches a class feature milestone to levels 5 and 10, a concept the advancement chapter explicitly rejects.
The advancement table (18-advancement.qmd:47) marks level 5 as a DP windfall, leaves level 10 milestone-free, and states classes do not have feature upgrades (line 56).
The Tower Shield row (22-reference-sheets.qmd:301) records only the DR bonus, dropping the half-cover property the armor chapter assigns.
The armor chapter grants the Tower Shield half cover alongside +3 DR (16-armor-shields.qmd:76).
Half Plate, Chain Mail, and Plate rows (22-reference-sheets.qmd:293-295) omit the 5-ft speed reduction the armor chapter attaches to all three.
Each of the three heavy armors reduces speed by 5 ft per the armor chapter (16-armor-shields.qmd:38-40).
Minor convention break: the career-DP range at line 228 uses a hyphen where the book's prose-range convention requires an en-dash.

Everything else checked holds against the authoritative chapters (skill roster and keys in ch07, discipline catalog in ch08, resolution, morale, dying, cover, economy, budgets, costs, armor DR values), so the refute is scoped to the named cells; the sheet's own intro frames these tables as the numbers used at the table, which is why contradictory cells are publish-blocking.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Quick-reference cells must never contradict their authoritative chapters.

payload.argument: The chapter fails as a publishable quick-reference unit: eight spots contradict the authoritative rules or teach arithmetic a rules-lawyer can exploit. (1) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:93] The Conditions table ends Prone with 'Stand up (move)', but the same page's maneuver list (line 70) and the combat chapter both treat standing as a Maneuver. Broken value: 'Stand up (move)'; expected: 'Stand up (maneuver)'; fix class: one-word consistency correction. Literal reading grants a free action-type per turn (stand via Movement, keep the Maneuver). (2) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:77] Asleep X is reduced to 'Unconscious', yet the sheet's own Unconscious row (line 97) means incapacitated, prone, and ended only by healing or a Medicine check; the combat chapter instead says asleep creatures are merely unaware for X minutes and wake on damage. Broken: 'Unconscious'; expected: 'Unaware for X minutes'; fix: restore authoritative wording. (3) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:277-279] For a level 3 party the encounter examples under-shoot their own budgets: four wolves (C1/2 each) total 2 against an Easy budget of 3; knight (C3) plus two guards (C1/2) total 4 against a Standard budget of 6; young dragon (C6) plus four cultists (C1/2) total 8 against a Hard budget of 9; only the Deadly row (ancient dragon, 12 vs 12) balances. Broken: example sums 2/4/8; expected: sums of 3/6/9; fix: rework the examples so totals match the multipliers (mirror table in the bestiary chapter needs the same pass). (4) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:221,226] The level table invents a 'Class feature' milestone at levels 5 and 10; the advancement chapter states classes get no feature upgrades, lists level 5 as a DP windfall, and level 10 as empty. Broken: 'Class feature'; expected: 'DP windfall' at 5 and no milestone at 10; fix: milestone relabel to match the authoritative table. (5) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:64] Aid loses its expiry: the combat chapter caps the bonus at 'before your next turn', the sheet does not, so the +2 can be banked across rounds. Broken: unbounded bonus; expected: deadline restored; fix: rule-fidelity wording. (6) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:65-66] Shove and Grapple are both flattened to opposed Brawn checks, deleting the defender's Agility option that the combat chapter guarantees (and, for grapples, the Athletics/Acrobatics skills); a high-Agility target is forced onto their worst stat. Broken: 'Opposed Brawn check' only; expected: Brawn vs Brawn/Agility, and Athletics-vs-Athletics-or-Acrobatics for grapples; fix: restore both defense options. (7) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:228] The 'approximately 50-52 career DP' estimate only holds when Knowledge plus Fortitude is at least +2, but those attributes may legally sum to -4, putting valid careers at 44-49; the creation chapter's own worked example lands at 48. Broken: fixed range; expected: the formula 48 + Knowledge + Fortitude (spanning 44-52); fix: restate as a formula. (8) [22-reference-sheets.qmd:303] PV is glossed as a defensive stance bonus, which fits Bastion (movement to enter stance) but not Arcane Shield (a free-action ward, once per round), so half the cited sources are misdescribed. Expected: PV as a +1 defense-roll bonus from either signature; fix: reword the gloss. Sections that survived stress-testing: all 23 skill keys, the discipline catalog, armor and shield values, damage budgets, dying/morale/cover, and DP costs are faithful to their source chapters - but the enumerated defects make the sheet unsafe to print as-is.

evidence.claim: The sheet's Conditions table tells a prone creature to stand up using its move, while the sheet's own maneuver list and the combat chapter's conditions table both classify standing up as a Maneuver.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Prone | Melee Boon vs you, ranged Bane | Stand up (move)

evidence.claim: The combat chapter defines being asleep as merely unaware for X minutes and waking on damage, a lighter state than the unconscious condition, which also includes incapacitated and prone and needs healing or medicine to end.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asleep X | Unaware for X minutes | Wakes on damage

evidence.claim: Against a level 3 party the sheet's Standard example totals 4 challenge points while the stated x2 budget is 6; the Easy and Hard examples similarly under-shoot, with only Deadly balancing.

The advancement chapter explicitly disclaims class feature upgrades, showing level 5 as a DP windfall and level 10 with no gains, so the sheet's two 'class feature' milestones point at rewards the game never grants.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Classes do not have feature upgrades

evidence.claim: The combat chapter's Aid maneuver expires when the helper's next turn arrives; the sheet drops that deadline, letting the bonus be held indefinitely.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: +2 on their next roll before your next turn

evidence.claim: The combat chapter lets a shoved target oppose with Agility rather than Brawn, and grapple contests use Athletics or Acrobatics; the sheet's Brawn-only shorthand strips those options.
Background DP equals 8 plus Knowledge plus Fortitude, and attribute rules let those two sum as low as -4, so total career DP can fall to 44-49, outside the sheet's stated 50-52 window.

Of the two signatures the sheet credits for PV, only Bastion is entered by spending movement; Arcane Shield is a free-action ward raised once per round, so the 'defensive stance' gloss fits only one of them.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Bastion, spend movement to enter a defensive stance

payload.argument: Refute: eight defects, all mechanical in scope, plus a set of verified-clean areas. (1) Line 9: the illustration caption still carries art-tracker residue ('Placeholder for final art'), which the book's cleanup precedent removes from captions. (2) Line 77: the Asleep X row labels the effect 'Unconscious'; the combat chapter says a sleeping creature is Unaware for X minutes and wakes on damage, and Unconscious is its own separate row in the same sheet. (3) Line 93: the Prone row ends with 'Stand up (move)', but rising is a maneuver per the combat chapter's Basic Maneuvers. (4) Level table cells: level 1's milestone wording drops 'Starting Disciplines' from the class-signature entry; levels 5 and 10 both say 'Class feature', yet the advancement chapter records no feature upgrades anywhere, gives level 5 a DP windfall, and leaves level 10's milestone cell empty. (5) Encounter examples under-fill three of four budgets for a level-3 party: four wolves total 2 against an Easy budget of 3; a knight plus two guards totals 4 against a Standard budget of 6; a young dragon plus four cultists totals 8 against a Hard budget of 9. Each needs six of the half-challenge minions (wolf, guard, cultist) to reach its budget; the Deadly row, one Ancient Dragon at 12, is correct. (6) Armor rows for Half Plate, Chain Mail, and Plate omit the 5 ft speed reduction the armor chapter imposes on each. (7) The Tower Shield row omits its half-cover property. (8) The defense summary calls PV a 'defensive stance bonus', while the glossary defines it as a temporary +1 bonus to the defense roll. Verified clean: all 23 skill keys including Craft and Alchemy match the skills chapter; the discipline catalog reproduces the full 23-discipline/9-category taxonomy; card costs (2/4/8) and the four discipline cost ladders match the economy; morale, dying, cover, trading, action-economy, damage-type, and damage-budget rows all match their source chapters; the Deadly example and the level-DP column totals are correct.

evidence.claim: Asleep X makes a creature Unaware for X minutes and it wakes on damage; it is not Unconscious.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Asleep X** | Unaware for X minutes | Wakes on damage

evidence.claim: The Prone condition's ends column specifies standing up as a maneuver.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Prone** | Melee Boon vs you, ranged Bane | Stand up (maneuver)

evidence.claim: Stand Up appears among the Basic Maneuvers, confirming rising costs a maneuver.
Level 1's milestone names the class signature plus Starting Disciplines.
Level 5's milestone is a DP windfall, not a class feature.
Level 10's row has no milestone entry at all.
The advancement chapter states classes receive no feature upgrades.

The Guard is Challenge 1/2, so six are needed with a C3 knight for a budget of 6.
The Cultist is Challenge 1/2, so six are needed with a C6 dragon for a budget of 9.
The Knight is Challenge 3.

The Ancient Dragon is Challenge 12, matching the Deadly row exactly.

evidence.claim: The chapter's illustration caption retains art-tracker placeholder residue that must be stripped.
Craft and Alchemy key to Reason in the skills chapter, matching the sheet's keys.
Card DP costs are 2/4/8 by tier, matching the sheet's DP Cost Reference.

evidence.claim: Novice damage bands are 2/4/6, matching the sheet's Damage Budget row.

payload.argument: Refute: the balance numbers themselves survive cell-by-cell checking, but the chapter breaks in four mechanics areas - example arithmetic, a damage-budget row label, progression milestone and total arithmetic, and maneuver/condition cells - nine defects total, each with a concrete broken value and expected value. (1) Encounter Building (lines 277-279): a level-3 party's budgets are 3/6/9/12 under the x1/x2/x3/x4+ multipliers, yet the Easy, Standard, and Hard examples sum to 2, 4, and 8 - Easy needs six wolves, Standard needs two knights (or a knight plus six guards), Hard needs a young dragon plus six cultists; only Deadly balances at 12. (2) Damage Budget label (line 267): the Novice row claims C1-2, but the bestiary assigns half-challenge creatures (wolf, bandit, guard, cultist, drowned guardian) and the challenge-1 dire wolf Novice damage, so the band must start at C1/2. (3) Level Progression (lines 221, 226): milestones at levels 5 and 10 say class feature, but the advancement chapter grants a DP windfall at 5, nothing at 10, and explicitly abolishes class feature upgrades. (4) Career-DP total (line 228): the real sum is 48 plus Knowledge plus Fortitude, so the claimed 50-52 window only materializes when those two attributes total at least +2; typical spreads land at 48-50. (5) Conditions (lines 77, 93): Asleep X is written as Unconscious although the combat chapter defines it as merely unaware for X minutes and the sheet already lists Unconscious as a heavier, separate row; Prone ends via a move although standing up is a maneuver per the combat chapter and the sheet's own line 70. (6) Maneuvers (lines 64-66): Aid omits the before-your-next-turn expiry, and Shove and Grapple restrict their contests to Brawn alone when the combat chapter lets the target oppose with Agility via Acrobatics. Verified clean: budget values 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21; card costs 2/4/8; discipline structures 1/2/4, 2/4/8, 3/6/12, 4/8/16; the 23-skill attribute keys; the 23-discipline nine-category catalog; morale, dying, cover, and armor/shield DR. A quick-reference chapter is the number set the table reaches for mid-session, so contradictory cells are publish-blocking; every fix is a cell-level correction.

evidence.claim: Encounter difficulty multiplies party level: x1 easy, x2 standard, x3 hard, x4+ deadly, which for a level-3 party yields budgets of 3, 6, 9, and 12.

evidence.claim: Easy example: four half-challenge wolves total 2 challenge points against an easy budget of 3; six wolves are the minimum count that reaches the budget.
Standard example: a 3-point knight plus two halves totals 4 against the 6-point standard budget; two knights, or a knight with six guards, would hit 6.
Hard example: a 6-point young dragon plus four halves totals 8 against the 9-point hard budget; six cultists instead of four would make 9.
The Damage Budget table labels the Novice row as challenge 1-2, silently excluding the half-challenge creatures the bestiary keys to Novice damage; the label should read C1/2-2.

Bestiary stat blocks put half-challenge wolves, bandits, guards, cultists, and drowned guardians, plus the challenge-1 dire wolf, all on the 2/4/6 Novice line, so the Novice band starts below challenge 1.
Levels 5 and 10 in the progression table both carry a class-feature milestone, a reward type the advancement chapter says the game no longer grants.
The advancement table lists level 5 as a DP windfall, leaves level 10 milestone-free, and states flatly that classes receive no feature upgrades.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Classes do not have feature upgrades

evidence.claim: The career-DP line claims a 50-52 total, but summing 32 advancement, 8 class, and background of 8 plus Knowledge plus Fortitude yields 48 plus those two attributes, so the stated window requires them to total at least +2.
The Asleep row's effect cell says Unconscious, duplicating the name of the heavier condition the sheet separately lists at line 97.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asleep X | Unconscious | X minutes or damage

evidence.claim: The combat chapter's condition table defines Asleep X as unaware for X minutes, waking on damage - a lighter state than the unconscious condition.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Asleep X | Unaware for X minutes | Wakes on damage

evidence.claim: The Prone row's ends cell directs standing up via movement, though the sheet's own maneuver table at line 70 lists Stand Up as a maneuver.
The combat chapter's Prone row ends via the Stand up maneuver, consistent with its basic maneuvers list.
The Aid entry grants a +2 to an ally's next roll with no stated expiry, letting the bonus sit unspent across multiple rounds.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Ally within 30 ft gains +2 on their next roll

evidence.claim: The combat chapter caps the Aid bonus at the helper's next turn, the expiry the sheet drops.
The Shove and Grapple rows both reduce their contests to Brawn alone.
The combat chapter lets a shoved or grappled target oppose with Brawn or Agility via Acrobatics at the target's choice, so Brawn-only shorthand removes a legal defense option.

Verified clean against the authoritative chapters: the 2/4/6, 6/9/12, 9/15/21 budget values; 2/4/8 card costs; 1/2/4, 2/4/8, 3/6/12, 4/8/16 discipline structures; 23 skill attribute keys; the 23-discipline nine-category catalog; morale, dying, cover, and armor/shield DR cells; so the refute is scoped to the nine named cells.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: All spells, abilities, and monster attacks use flat damage values

payload.argument: On voice the chapter holds: the register is terse, direct, and matches the book's punchy tone, and the big-ticket cross-checks pass — the 23-skill roster with attribute keys, the success-tier bands, the difficulty ladder, the flat damage budgets, and the creation checklist all agree with their authoritative chapters. What fails is abbreviation discipline and vocabulary consistency, precisely where a quick reference is most dangerous. Five named things get renamed or mislabeled: the sleep condition's effect is written as the Unconscious state, which collides with the separate Unconscious condition row on the same page and contradicts the combat chapter; the prone row's recovery is called a move even though rising is a maneuver in both the combat chapter and this sheet's own maneuver table; the aid, shove, and grapple rows drop the expiry clause or the defender's Agility option, changing what the rule allows; the level table invents a 'class feature' milestone at levels 5 and 10, a concept the advancement chapter never grants, and renames the Progression Discipline milestone; and Protection Value is described as a stance bonus when the glossary defines it as a flat defense-roll bonus. The item tables also understate: the tower shield omits its half-cover benefit and the armor table omits the heavy-armor speed penalty. A reference sheet is allowed to compress details, but it may not change a rule's meaning or give one thing two names; because two of these defects set the sheet's own tables against each other, the chapter must change. Every fix is a localized vocabulary swap, single-cell edit, or small table addition — mechanical class, no structural rewrite.

evidence.claim: The sleep row names its effect as the Unconscious state, but the combat chapter defines it as unaware for a number of minutes, and the same sheet also lists a distinct Unconscious condition, so one state is given two names and one name is overloaded.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: **Asleep X** | Unconscious | X minutes or damage

evidence.claim: The prone row's end condition bills rising as a movement, while the combat chapter and this sheet's own basic maneuver list both treat rising as a maneuver; the wording would let a player spend Movement to stand.
The aid row drops the expiry clause present in the combat chapter, so the +2 appears to linger until the ally next rolls instead of ending at your following turn.
The shove row frames the contest as Brawn-only, but the combat chapter lets the defender oppose with Agility instead, so the sheet narrows who can resist the push.
The grapple row inlines the same Brawn-only contest, while the combat chapter's grappling rules let the target oppose with Brawn or Agility of their choosing.

Three level rows rename the advancement milestone as a generic rank increase, but the advancement chapter names it Progression Discipline and tallies three of them by level 10, giving one milestone two labels across the book.
Levels 5 and 10 are credited with a class feature, a milestone that does not exist: the advancement chapter grants a DP windfall at 5, nothing at 10, and states classes have no feature upgrades.

The defense summary rebrands Protection Value as a stance bonus, but the glossary defines it as a temporary +1 to the defense roll from the same two named abilities, so the sheet's phrasing implies a posture rather than a flat bonus.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Protection Value (PV) is a defensive stance bonus

evidence.claim: The tower shield row lists only the discipline requirement and DR bonus, dropping the half-cover benefit (and the carrying speed cost) the armor chapter attaches to the item, understating the shield.

The armor table omits the 5 ft speed penalty that the armor chapter applies to half plate, chain mail, and plate, and likewise skips the spellcasting penalties for heavier armors, so a player building from the sheet never learns heavy armor slows them.

The career-DP summary uses a plain hyphen in a prose range while the same chapter uses en-dashes in the damage-budget tier labels, so the sheet is internally inconsistent on range punctuation against the book's standing convention.

payload.argument: Final-quality audit of the quick-reference chapter finds it is not publishable as written. The sheet's spine is largely faithful to its authoritative sources: the 23-skill roster and attribute keys match ch07, the discipline catalog (23 disciplines across 9 categories) matches ch08, the difficulty ladder matches ch06, the morale/dying/cover/effects tables match ch13, the damage budget and card/discipline costs match the standing conventions, and the creation checklist (order, +3 attribute total, background DP formula, ancestries, derived stats) matches ch02. However, six cells are broken in the sense that a reader will act on wrong information: the level-5 and level-10 milestones announce a class feature that the advancement chapter explicitly rules out; the Shove and Asleep X entries misstate mechanics; the Prone end-condition contradicts the sheet's own maneuver table; and the Easy/Standard/Hard encounter examples sum to 2/4/8 against level-3 budgets of 3/6/9. The opening caption also retains the art-tracker placeholder sentence the book convention strips (ch20 precedent). Beyond that, nine load-bearing details are incomplete: the Aid expiry qualifier, the grapple resistance options, the heavy-armor speed penalty, the tower shield's half-cover property, the Protection Value definition drift, the dropped Starting Disciplines grant at level 1, a hyphen that must be an en-dash plus an over-optimistic career-DP band, and the absence of any defense-roll procedure despite the sheet referencing Defense rolls twice. Two of these are internal contradictions within the same sheet (Asleep X vs Unconscious; Prone end vs Stand Up maneuver). Fix classes: nearly all are mechanical cell-level corrections; the defense-roll table is the only substantive insertion. Note for the synthesis: ch20's mirror encounter table carries the same wrong sums and should be re-totalled in the same pass.

evidence.claim: The opening illustration caption (line 9) still carries the art-tracker placeholder sentence that the standing convention strips from captions, following the bestiary chapter's precedent.

The level-5 milestone (line 221) and the level-10 milestone (line 226) both promise a 'Class feature', a reward category the advancement chapter states does not exist; level 10 should have no milestone at all.

The authoritative level table marks level 5 as a plain DP bonus with no feature and leaves level 10 empty, and its design note rules out class feature upgrades entirely, so both sheet cells are broken.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: Classes do not have feature upgrades

evidence.claim: The example encounters under-fill their budgets: Easy (line 277) totals 2 against a level-3 budget of 3, Standard (line 278) totals 4 against 6, and Hard (line 279) totals 8 against 9, since Wolves, Guards, and Cultists are each Challenge 1/2; only the Deadly row (line 280) sums correctly to 12.

The GM chapter defines each difficulty as a multiplier of party level with creature Challenge as the budget unit, so the corrected rows need six half-challenge creatures, a knight plus six guards, and a young dragon plus six cultists to reach 3, 6, and 9; the same wrong sums appear in the bestiary chapter's mirror table.

evidence.claim: The Shove row (line 65) reduces resistance to a Brawn-only contest; the combat chapter lets the target resist with Brawn or Agility, so the expected text is 'Opposed Brawn vs Brawn/Agility'.

payload.argument: The chapter holds up structurally on most layout axes: heading levels stay within the allowed three tiers with no skipped depths, every table renders inside the text column with nothing clipped (verified in the built PDF), the tier-band shorthand keeps its correct hyphen forms, and the chapter contains zero em-dashes. However, three presentation defects ship in the built book. (1) The opening caption at 22-reference-sheets.qmd:9 still carries a production tracker clause naming placeholder art and its source-file dimensions; the built PDF page 351 prints that clause and even breaks the filename across two lines. This contradicts the accepted ch20 disposition that stripped such clauses while keeping the italic caption. (2) The prose range at 22-reference-sheets.qmd:228 uses a hyphen where the book's prose-range standard calls for an en-dash; the built PDF page 362 prints the hyphenated form. (3) Two subsection headings inside the combat block orphan at page bottoms: the conditions heading lands alone at the foot of PDF page 355 with its 21-row table starting on page 356, and the effects heading plus its intro paragraph sit at the foot of page 356 with the table beginning on page 357. On a chapter whose stated purpose is tear-out table reference, a heading separated from its own table breaks scanability. Render checks answer the open questions: no table column is at overflow risk (longest cell, the Parry key-use entry, wraps to three lines without clipping), and no footnote is missing (the closing summary already explains the armor, PV, and shield terms). Fix scope: strip the caption clause per precedent, swap in the en-dash, and bind the orphaned headings to their tables (pagebreak before the subsection or a keep-with-next rule) so the fix survives a clean build.

payload.rationale: Topic t-01 rejected 7-0 in round 1 (f-001..f-007 all refute, un-rebutted; quorum 4, reject_quorum 4). The chapter's spine is faithful (23-skill roster + keys match ch07; discipline catalog 23/9 matches ch08; damage budget values, card costs 2/4/8, discipline structures, difficulty ladder, morale, dying, cover, effects, damage types all match their sources) - the refutes are tightly scoped to arithmetic, vocabulary, and two layout defects. Encounter-example arithmetic (2/4/8 vs budgets 3/6/9) was independently verified by five lenses and by direct computation; the mirror table in ch20 shares the flaw and the ch20 run's claim that it was fixed is disproven by the file (verify-before-trust: the file is the source of record). 'Class feature' milestones at L5/L10 contradict ch18's explicit 'Classes do not have feature upgrades' and the level table (L5 = DP windfall, L10 = no milestone). 'Novice (C1-2)' omits the C1/2 tier that ch20's own minions occupy. Asleep/Prone wording collides with the sheet's own condition rows and ch13. The layout-expert verified the caption residue and the orphaned subsection headings against the built PDF via pdftotext (pp.351/355-357/362). Researcher's PV-wording item aligns ch22:303 to the ch21 glossary definition locked earlier today (PR #388).
